questions.question_text:
A simple interest investment of $\$3000$ at $6\%$ p.a. is graphed with interest $I$ against time $t$.
What is the interest earned after $5$ years?

options.why: Calculated interest for one year instead of five years.
Calculated the total amount rather than the interest earned.
Applied the interest rate as 0.6 rather than 0.06.

questions.question_text:
An investment of $\$2400$ earns simple interest at $5\%$ p.a.
What is the total balance $A$ shown on the balance-time graph after $3$ years?

options.why: Gave only the interest earned without adding the principal.
Calculated balance after one year instead of three years.
Used four years of interest instead of three.

questions.question_text:
Three simple interest graphs for a $\$2000$ principal have gradients $80$, $120$, and $160$.
Which line represents an annual interest rate of $8\%$ p.a.?

options.why: Gradient 80 corresponds to a 4% interest rate.
Gradient 120 corresponds to a 6% interest rate.
Confused the vertical intercept with the gradient.

questions.question_text:
Two investments earn simple interest at $4\%$ p.a.
Line $A$ has gradient $200$ and Line $B$ has gradient $120$.
What is the principal for Line $A$?

options.why: Calculated the principal for Line B instead of Line A.
Added the principals together.
Divided by 0.4 instead of 0.04.

questions.question_text:
A simple interest graph for a $\$6000$ investment passes through $(4, 1440)$.
What is the annual interest rate?

options.why: Did not divide by the four-year time period.
Substituted time incorrectly into the formula.
Forgot to convert the decimal rate into a percentage.

questions.question_text:
Option $A$ earns simple interest on $\$4000$ at $7\%$ p.a.
Option $B$ earns simple interest on $\$4000$ at $4\%$ p.a.
What is the difference in interest earned after $5$ years?

options.why: Calculated the difference in interest for only one year.
Calculated total interest for Option A only.
Calculated total interest for Option B only.

questions.question_text:
A balance graph for a simple interest account passes through $(3, 4720)$ and $(6, 5440)$.
What is the annual interest rate?

options.why: Used final balance instead of principal to find rate.
Divided gradient by the balance at year 3.
Incorrectly calculated annual interest increment.

questions.question_text:
Investment $1$ ($P = \$8000, r = 3\%$ p.a.) and Investment $2$ ($P = \$5000, r = 6\%$ p.a.) earn simple interest.
After how many years will Investment $2$ have earned $\$900$ more interest than Investment $1$?

options.why: Calculated time for a 600 dollar difference.
Used sum of rates rather than difference in annual earnings.
Divided by annual rate instead of difference in earnings.
